title: Tow occurrence and positive-catch density did not show clear dominance in Northeast Shelf thermal tracking
abstract: We split annual plankton density change into additive occurrence and positive-catch density parts. We used NOAA EcoMon tows in 1992-2023, with early spatial slopes fixed before later outcomes. The primary sample had 65 zooplankton cells and 60 fish-larva cells. Incidence and density transfer estimates were 0.297 and 0.306 for zooplankton, and 0.248 and 0.771 for fish larvae. Paired differences had 97.5% crossed-bootstrap intervals of -0.871 to 0.259 and -2.929 to 0.358. Neither showed clear dominance. Coverage and zero-endpoint checks kept this uncertainty. An abundance-only Poisson model on fixed spatial support can give either occurrence-dominated or density-dominated change. Thus tow occurrence does not by itself identify colonisation. The study adds an exact split, paired tests and a proof of an observation limit. It reuses one survey and prior methods. Sparse seasons, few blocks, coarse taxa and unknown detection limit inference. It does not identify a causal climate effect or the process that sets the terrestrial gap.

display.caption: The exact split of thermal transfer and paired differences, with 97.5% marginal intervals. The right panel shows an abundance-only model on fixed spatial support. Occurrence change need not show colonisation.
